issues.description: Imports().DescriptorProto() still dereferences i.publicEnd via the returned closure on nil receiver
issues.detail: In ir_imports.go Directs(), when i==nil, slice is empty so the Indexer body never runs — fine. But Transitive() and Directs() closures capture `i` and read i.publicEnd / i.importEnd inside the mapper. The empty slice saves you today, but the next refactor that drops the length guard will crash. Either bail out earlier returning an empty Indexer, or assert non-nil at the top.

issues.description: THREE-PATCHES: zero-test addition is mixed with ~20 behavioral nil-guard fixes in one commit
issues.detail: The description says "adds a zero test... also fixes panics." That's two patches. The taste is to land the test first (red), then each panic fix as its own diff with a one-line justification. As submitted, a bisect on any future regression in File.Imports() points at "add zero test" — useless. Maintainer-six-years-from-now curses you.

issues.description: BAD-TASTE: every accessor now opens with a hand-rolled nil/IsZero special case
issues.detail: Twenty-plus methods grow the same `var x T; if f != nil { x = f.field }; return seq.NewFixedSlice(x, ...)` boilerplate. The good-taste fix is one helper — e.g. make seq.NewFixedSlice tolerate a nil receiver path, or add a `(f *File) slice[T](...)` helper that handles nil once. You eliminated the panics by adding a special case everywhere instead of removing the special case.

issues.description: Reflection-driven test silently skips methods with parameters and treats any Len()==0 as success
issues.detail: testZeroAny filters to NumIn()==1, so any accessor that takes an argument (e.g. ImportFor) is never exercised on the zero value. And the Len() probe assumes any type with a Len method is a container — fine today, fragile tomorrow. Add an explicit allowlist of skipped methods so future accessors don't silently escape the test.

issues.description: ValueNodeIndex sentinel -1 is undocumented in the type and inconsistent with the rest of the API
issues.detail: Every other zero accessor returns the zero value of the return type. ValueNodeIndex returns -1 for zero, which means callers now need to know two sentinels (0 valid, -1 zero). Either document this on Element itself (not just a doc-comment line) or return 0 and require callers to check IsZero. Pick one convention.

issues.description: AllMembers index counter `i` is captured before the nil-guard short-circuit and is dead on nil path
issues.detail: Cosmetic, but the `i := 0` line sits above the iterx.Map regardless of whether raw is nil. It works because Map over a nil seq yields nothing, but the diff reads worse than the original. Hoist the whole body into the `if f != nil` branch and return an empty seq otherwise — fewer lines, clearer intent.

review.summary: NEEDS-WORK. The test is fine — actually good; a reflection-driven zero-value sweep is exactly the kind of cheap structural check more codebases should have. The problem is everything around it. This is at least two patches glued together: the test, and a wide spray of nil/IsZero guards across the IR accessors. Land them separately so bisect stays useful. And the guards themselves are bad-taste: the same five-line boilerplate copied into twenty methods instead of one helper that makes nil-receiver iteration a non-event. Fix the shape, then this lands.
